title: Unicode paths, names and cross-platform product regression
product_schema: apps/reader/store/001_catalog.sql (application_id 1163416144, user_version 1), unchanged since the implementation start

accepted.workflow: Unicode paths names and cross-platform product regression

areas.note: identical counts on all three hosts; one record is one frozen observation

cross_platform.comparison: parsed observations compared record by record and field by field

observed_guarantees: reader_command_utf16 accepts the 42 frozen payloads it should accept and refuses NUL, unpaired surrogates, 16385 UTF-16 units, a 16388-byte result and a too small capacity, always leaving bytes=0

import rejects invalid UTF-8 (lone continuation, overlong, truncated, surrogate, above U+10FFFF), 4097 scalars, an unknown format, an uppercase digest, favorite=2, a byte length that disagrees with the retained original and an SDK ID already mapped to another original

typed commands keep created/applied, entity keys and revision digests exact; an exact retry is a 0/0 no-op before the stale-head check; a retained ID with different bytes is COLLISION; 4097 scalars is LIMIT; truncated UTF-8 is FORMAT; a delete without observed history is ARGUMENT; a missing book history is NEEDS_BOOK_BOOTSTRAP

catalog pages follow (sort_title, book_key) byte order for CJK, emoji, NFC, NFD, Hebrew, Russian, Arabic, RTL controls, reserved characters, tab/newline and an empty sort title, including 16384-byte and 12288-byte keys, in both directions and across continued keyset pages
search folds ASCII A-Z only: 'abc' hits 'ABC', 'UNI-with-diaeresis' (uppercase) does not hit the lowercase form, and an NFD query hits an NFD field because the bytes are exact
sub-shelves order by (ordinal,id), tags and series by id, members by (ordinal,book_key) or book_key, soft deletion hides rows, keeps the name, and exposes only removed groups

every retained revision is returned byte for byte with a SHA-256 that covers exactly those bytes; receipts with a wrong digest, a flipped byte, invalid UTF-8 or a truncation are refused without writing
a mirror database built only from received revisions and projected head by head reaches the same catalog state as the writer
closing and reopening both stores reproduces every recorded byte, key, order and selection state
JSON escape sequences are decoded for meaning (U+00E9, U+1F4DA, U+0009) while the retained revision bytes stay exactly as received
the whole session runs on a Unicode directory and database name supplied through reader_command_utf16, and both observers report identical observations on Windows, Linux and macOS
not_granted: typography, bidi visual ordering, line breaking and glyph selection are not measured
screen-reader or accessibility behaviour is not measured
the host side NFC conversion itself (NormalizeString or g_utf8_normalize) is not exercised; the frozen NFC form is supplied as the documented host input
the SDK-bound desktop adapter reader_catalog_sdk_* is not built; attach is called with host-verified frozen identity as documented
performance, CPU and the existing numeric budgets are untouched and unmeasured
no real user document and no legacy 1710 target is included in this package count

earlier_runs.cause: consumer called reader_catalog_remove_local with two arguments instead of three (all three hosts, same diagnostic)
fixture generator raised KeyError 'sha': the modelled book dict lacked the original digest
fixture generator raised KeyError 'path.workdir': path items were read from a removed aux namespace

one of 359 records differed on all hosts: cmd.neg.collision reported UNSAFE because the fixture reused no retained revision ID, so the case never reached the collision branch; the checker also miscounted row fields
earlier_runs.note: the underlying observation was reproduced identically on all three hosts

earlier_runs.cause: all three consumer jobs passed 359/359 and 8/8, but the comparison found different frozen fixture digests: Windows wrote the JSON fixtures with CRLF line endings

earlier_runs.note: first fully green run; superseded by the accepted run only because it does not print the named per-area counts and consumer digests
